title: Assemble one line

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Write the heart of an assembler for the tiny computer of 4.04:

```python
def assemble_line(text, labels)     # one instruction as text -> its number
```

- `text` is an instruction name and an operand, such as `"LOAD 10"` or `"JUMPZ done"`, or just `"HALT"` (which is 0).
- The operand is a number, or a label: look labels up in the `labels` dictionary, which maps names to cell numbers.
- Names may be in any case: `"load 10"` is fine.

```python
assemble_line("LOAD 10", {})                 # 110
assemble_line("JUMPZ done", {"done": 5})     # 605
assemble_line("store counter", {"counter": 6})   # 406
```

`text.split()` splits on spaces; `name.upper()` gives the upper-case name; `operand.isdigit()` tells a number from a label.

solution.solution.py:
NAMES = ["HALT", "LOAD", "ADD", "SUB", "STORE", "JUMP", "JUMPZ"]

def assemble_line(text, labels):
    parts = text.split()
    name = parts[0].upper()
    if name == "HALT":
        return 0
    operand = parts[1]
    address = int(operand) if operand.isdigit() else labels[operand]
    return NAMES.index(name) * 100 + address
